page: Microsoft Azure M416-208ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8280L processor with an x86_64 architecture, delivering 104 physical cores and 208 dedicated vCPUs at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The server is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 11400.0 GB, which equates to 54.81 GB per core, and includes 8389 GB of local storage with no integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25%, the massive core count drives multi-core performance into the top 10% tier. This is demonstrated by top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Additionally, the server exhibits exceptional memory bandwidth, with both cached and uncached read and write operations ranking in the top 10%, alongside a top-tier Redis SET performance of 159.37 million operations per second.

Given its extreme resource density and massive memory footprint, this server represents a highly specialized hardware class designed for scale rather than budget efficiency. It is ideally suited for massive in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise applications, data warehousing, and heavy multi-threaded workloads that require substantial RAM and high memory bandwidth, rather than single-threaded processing speed.
